why: This file searched the extraction MODELS' NOTES for a claimed portfolio transfer and reported 81 records carrying no RITC flag. A model's narrative mentions 'commutation' or 'quota share' in accounting-policy boilerplate and in passing description, so prose matching counts mentions, not events. The deterministic scanner reads the filings themselves and reports 10 flagged syndicate-years, 4 of which are not already flagged as RITC; every one of the 10 was read by hand before the count was published. Do not quote the 81.
kept_because: It is how the question was found, and the difference between 81 and 10 is itself the argument against keying a flag on model prose.

original.purpose: Records whose extraction notes claim a portfolio transfer of prior-year liabilities -- a quota share, loss portfolio transfer, novation or commutation. Such a transfer moves another party's claims into this syndicate's gross triangle, so the triangle's diagonal is not purely its own development. Reinsurance-to-close has its own scanner and its own regime in the fitted model; these do not.
original.round: round 56 (R166), found while adjudicating the override-gate change
original.status: OPEN. The adopted figures are unchanged: a claim in a model's prose is not evidence, the filings concerned are scanned so the claim cannot be checked without OCR, and two prompt versions gave different reasons for distrusting the same triangle. This is a review list and a countable limitation, not a correction.
